item.text:
**7B.7 Research Note: Bongbong Marcos in 2024**  
Assessment: **mixed, leaning negative**. Marcos allowed some domestic procedural checks and anti-graft actions, but he also refused meaningful external scrutiny of the drug war, while red-tagging, media pressure, and politically connected influence remained active.

**Positive evidence**
- **PBBM says Comelec has mandate to probe alleged signature-buying for PI**. *Philippine News Agency*, January 23, 2024. [URL](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1217440)  
  Marcos said he would not meddle with Comelec’s inquiry into alleged signature-buying for the people’s initiative drive. That is real deference to an independent election body.  
  QIDs: **7B.7, 7B.6**

- **Gov’t vows legal action vs deep fake video creators, spreaders**. *Presidential Communications Office*, April 26, 2024. [URL](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/govt-vows-legal-action-vs-deep-fake-video-creators-spreaders/)  
  The government said DICT and NSC were investigating the manipulated Marcos deepfake and considering legal action. This is a defensive institutional response, not a cover-up.  
  QIDs: **7B.7, 7B.6**

- **PBBM stands by suspension of 139 NFA officials**. *Presidential Communications Office*, March 6, 2024. [URL](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-stands-by-suspension-of-139-nfa-officials/)  
  Marcos backed suspensions over anomalous rice sales and procedural irregularities inside the NFA. That is evidence of disciplining subordinates rather than shielding them.  
  QIDs: **7B.7, 7B.4**

- **DOJ creates task force to review EJK cases**. *Philippine News Agency*, November 6, 2024. [URL](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1237266)  
  The DOJ formed a task force to review Duterte-era EJKs, case-build, and file charges if warranted. This is a genuine accountability step, though it was executive-led and focused on the previous administration.  
  QIDs: **7B.7, 7B.6**

- **Philippines: Supreme Court Rejects ‘Red-Tagging’**. *Human Rights Watch*, May 8, 2024. [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/08/philippines-supreme-court-rejects-red-tagging)  
  The Supreme Court ruled red-tagging threatens life, liberty, and security. In the 2024 record I reviewed, Marcos did not retaliate against the ruling, which is modest evidence of tolerating judicial constraint.  
  QIDs: **7B.7, 7B.6**

**Negative evidence**
- **No PH cooperation with ICC unless PRRD wants it – PBBM**. *Presidential Communications Office*, November 14, 2024. [URL](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/no-ph-cooperation-with-icc-unless-prrd-wants-it-pbbm/)  
  Marcos said the Philippines would not cooperate with the ICC investigation of the Duterte drug war. That is the clearest direct evidence of refusing independent external scrutiny.  
  QIDs: **7B.7, 7B.6**

- **Philippines: ‘Red-Tagging’ Puts Activists at Risk**. *Human Rights Watch*, January 11, 2024. [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/philippines-red-tagging-puts-activists-risk)  
  HRW said officials and supporters used media to accuse critics of insurgent ties, placing activists at serious risk. That supports a finding of tolerated intimidation of investigators and critics.  
  QIDs: **7B.7, 7B.2, 7B.6**

- **Philippines: Dangerous ‘Red Tagging’ of Labor Leaders**. *Human Rights Watch*, September 25, 2024. [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/25/philippines-dangerous-red-tagging-labor-leaders)  
  HRW reported officials, police, and military members repeatedly threatened union leaders by accusing them of communist links. This is direct evidence of coercive pressure on civic actors who can expose abuse.  
  QIDs: **7B.7, 7B.2, 7B.6**

- **Philippines: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report**. *Freedom House*, 2024. [URL](https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-world/2024)  
  Freedom House says campaign-finance rules are weak and poorly enforced, and patronage/kinship still shape political power. That is structural evidence that scrutiny of money, donors, and conflicts of interest remains constrained.  
  QIDs: **7B.7, 7B.6, 7B.5**

- **Philippines: Digital News Report 2024**. *Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism*, June 17, 2024. [URL](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines)  
  The report describes persistent red-tagging, libel pressure, blocked sites, and political pressure on media, alongside politically connected business activity involving the Romualdez family. That is strong background evidence of a still-coercive scrutiny environment.  
  QIDs: **7B.7, 7B.6, 7B.5, 7B.4**

**Search gap**
- I did **not** find reliable 2024 evidence that Marcos directly ordered destruction of records, fired auditors/prosecutors for digging too hard, or explicitly neutralized the courts in his own or his family’s cases.
- The strongest negative evidence is therefore **selective non-cooperation and tolerated coercion**, not a clean, documented command to bury evidence.
